text: I'm in this crowded station, it's so loud, people everywhere, just talking over each other, can't focus, it's like the noise is closing in, lights are too bright, feeling really overstimulated right now, just needed to step aside for a moment, don't know how to shake this feeling off, everything's too much

so today was really nice, like I woke up and just felt lighter, not sure why, but it’s such a change from the last few flat grey days, everything felt heavy and dull, and now it’s like there's this little spark again, kind of disbelieving honestly, wondering if it’s real or just a fluke, need to remember this feeling because when the grey days come back I always forget that the good ones happen too...

so today was kind of strange, like I spent hours just wandering around, not doing much of anything, just kind of letting time slip by, and then suddenly in the last thirty minutes I got a burst of energy or something, like I tackled that bug in the app that had been sitting there forever and just knocked it out, don't really get why it happens like that but it's like I need to run out of time before I can focus, it's weird, but I want to remember this, how it shifts from nothing to everything all at once

so it's Sunday evening again and here comes that familiar low dread creeping in, like clockwork, honestly it’s getting kind of weird how this keeps happening, I mean it’s like every Sunday night I just feel this weight, maybe it’s just the thought of the week ahead or something but it’s really starting to feel like a routine, I don't know if I’m just overthinking it or if there’s actually something to it, but I want to keep track of it, see if it really is weekly, just feels like I should note it down or something... I guess I'll just have to see

so here we are again, another Sunday evening and I can feel that low dread creeping in, it's different this time though, more about the week ahead, the pressure of unfinished work looming over me, kind of like a ticking clock, I thought I might escape it today but nope, same pattern as always, why does this happen every week, I wonder if there's something about Sundays that just makes me feel this way, like a reminder that the weekend's almost over and Monday's coming, just wish I knew how to shake it off

so it's sunday evening and I'm just feeling this low mood creeping in, don't know why, nothing specific just this weight, like the week is looming or something, I guess it's just the thought of tomorrow, but it's not like I have anything major coming up, just this dread I can't shake off

so I just remembered I need to cancel that gym membership before it renews next week, also gotta call the insurance company about the claim, they said to do it by Friday, it's just been on my mind and I keep forgetting

so I finally did that form I've been avoiding for like weeks, seriously can't believe I put it off for so long, it took me twenty minutes, twenty minutes after all that time, just sat down and did it, why do I make things so hard for myself sometimes

so I just got back from my walk, that's the third time this week, which is kind of awesome, I mean, I don't want to jinx it or anything but it feels good to keep this streak going, like it’s just a small thing but it adds up, you know? I really hope I can keep it up for the rest of the week, fingers crossed

so it's the second time this week doing the habit, got up early again, went for the walk, and did the practice session, feeling pretty good about it, building the count, that's two now, just need to keep this momentum going... not sure why it's easier this time, maybe just getting used to it

so today I actually did the habit for the first time this week, didn't think I'd get to it but here we are, felt really good to finally check that off, like it was a weight lifted or something, didn't expect to feel this way about it, just kinda nice to get back into it

so tired but can't sleep, mind won't stop — thinking about that meeting today, the code that broke, the conversation with jess, did i say the right thing? just wanna switch off but it’s like everything is looping, like a broken record, ugh
Mood: neutral - woke up feeling a bit restless, maybe too much screen time last night.

Felt really irritable this afternoon, not sure why — could be the slow website, that poorly worded message I got, or even just someone chewing loudly nearby. It all just piled up, and I didn't even notice until later. Kind of embarrassing to realize I let little things get to me like that. Maybe it's just stress from other stuff I haven't dealt with? Not sure but definitely something to think about.

I'm so nervous right now. Waiting for this call. It’s always like this. The waiting is worse than the call itself. I know it, but it doesn’t help. My heart is racing. I keep thinking about what I’ll say, what they'll ask. Will I mess up? I do this every time. It never gets easier. Why do I put myself through this? I want to just get it over with, but here I am, just waiting. It’s like I’m stuck in this loop. Can’t focus on anything else. Just this anxiety. Ugh.

Today was one of those scattered days where I opened like five different things and started three of them but didn't finish a single one. I’ve got tabs for a blog post about productivity tips, a half-written message to a friend that I just couldn't get the words right for, and a task list that I just kept rewriting instead of actually doing anything on it. It's like I’m just moving things around instead of making progress. I even started looking into that new API I want to integrate but got distracted halfway through. I know writing this is just another way of avoiding the actual tasks but it feels good to get it out. Maybe I just need to be kinder to myself about days like this. It happens, right? Sometimes you just need to breathe and reset. Tomorrow is another chance to do better.

It's interesting to look back over the past few days and see the same theme popping up in my notes. I keep circling around this worry, almost like I'm avoiding it but also can't help but acknowledge it. At the same time, there are these small moments of joy that break through, fleeting but real. It's like I'm in this loop, reflecting on these feelings over and over again. I thought I was being productive, but maybe I'm just going in circles. Why do I keep returning to these same thoughts, and what does that say about where I'm at right now?

Tonight was quiet. I cooked pasta with garlic and olive oil, added some spinach I had left. The kitchen smelled nice. I took my time, no rush. After dinner, I tidied up a corner of the living room, just moved some books around. It felt good to organize. I left my phone in the bedroom, no notifications, just silence. I sat on the couch for a while, looking out the window. The street was calm, just a few cars. I enjoyed the stillness. Nothing happened, and that was nice. Just a good ordinary evening.

So I moved my workspace to the coffee shop down the street and shifted my hours to start later in the day, dropped that early morning meeting I dreaded. I thought it would feel liberating, like I’d finally have the freedom to work when I’m most productive, but honestly, it’s been a mixed bag. The first few days were great, I felt energized and excited, but then I started to miss the structure of my old routine, like I’m not sure when to take breaks and I end up working way too long without realizing it. It’s only been a week, so I know I need to give it more time, but I’m surprised how much I miss that early morning quiet time. I’ll keep an eye on my productivity and mood over the next few weeks to see if this really works for me or if I need to adjust again.

I keep thinking about that offhand remark someone made the other day, they said I have a knack for making complex things simple, didn’t really expect it to hit me the way it did. It felt like a compliment but also made me question if I actually believe it myself. I mean, do I really simplify things or just gloss over the details? Maybe they saw something in me that I don’t see, or maybe it was just a nice thing to say in passing. Why does it resonate so much? Is it because I struggle with confidence in my skills? I want to be fair to them, they probably didn’t mean to leave me pondering, but it’s stuck, and now I’m here trying to dissect it.

Pick up dry cleaning
Return library books
Book dentist appointment - next week
Get groceries - milk, eggs, bread
Buy new phone charger
I still owe Sarah a reply about the project updates. Opened her email four times now and just can't seem to find the right words. Need to get this off my mind, it’s annoying me.

Found a tool called Notion AI that could help streamline my note-taking process, heard it's pretty intuitive and might save me time. Not urgent though, I can check it out at some point when I have time.
Renewal deadline: 2023-11-15. Need to submit the insurance renewal form by this date to avoid lapses. Don't forget to double-check the payment options before submitting.

finish that feature for the app, call mom, laundry, update resume, send that email to the client, buy groceries, research new tech stack, fix the bug in the code, plan weekend trip, clean the kitchen, remember to water the plants, get a haircut, prep for the meeting, organize files, schedule dentist appointment, need to follow up on that project, read that book on productivity, oh and don’t forget to check in with the team, wow this is a lot, maybe just writing it down helps, feels lighter already but where to even start...
Finally closed the tax return task that had been hanging around for about 6 months. Moved it from list to list way too many times (never again).

I just hit my 10th project completion, and this time I did it all on my own. It took a lot of late nights and pushing through self-doubt, but I’m proud of how far I've come. This is a big deal for me, feeling like I can handle things solo now.

It's interesting to reflect on how I used to dread debugging code, it felt like pulling teeth, hours spent wrestling with errors that seemed impossible to crack. I remember sitting for days on a single issue, feeling so overwhelmed. But now, I just fixed a bug in a couple of minutes without even breaking a sweat. It’s like my brain has rewired itself to handle these challenges more efficiently. I hardly even noticed the change until now, but debugging has become just another part of the process, a task that feels almost effortless. Progress is subtle but real.
Walked 1.5 miles today, which is more than I usually do. Cooked a healthy dinner instead of ordering takeout again. Not huge, but it feels good to take these little steps!

Today, my colleague said, 'You really nailed that project, your attention to detail made a huge difference.' It felt really good to hear that, kind of awkward to write it down but I know I need to keep this for later. I often forget these little wins and they really help boost my confidence. So saving it here to remind myself that I’m doing well sometimes, even when I doubt it. Need to remember to celebrate these moments more.
